shops.name: Johnstown, County Kildare
shops.description: Johnstown (Irish: Baile Eoin) is a village in County Kildare, Ireland. It is located 2 km (1.2 mi) north of Naas just off the N7 at junction 8. It is approximately 25 km (16 mi) from Dublin city centre, and is a home for commuters working in Dublin and Naas. Most of the housing was built after 1990. shops.name: Streamstown, County Westmeath
shops.description: Streamstown (Irish: Baile an tSrutháin) is a village in County Westmeath, Ireland. It sits roughly 20 km from the county town of Mullingar. Streamstown was historically called Ballintruhan, which is an anglicisation of its Irish name. shops.name: Glenealy, County Wicklow
shops.description: Glenealy (Irish: Gleann Fhaidhle) is a village in County Wicklow, Ireland. It is 8 km (5 mi) west of Wicklow Town, on the R752 road. The Dublin–Rosslare railway line also passes through the village. The village is in a civil parish of the same name. shops.name: Mick Finnegan
shops.description: Mick Finnegan is a former president of the Workers' Party. He was elected to that position on 17 May 2008 at the party's Annual Conference and retired in 2014. Finnegan is originally from near Bailieborough, County Cavan, but has spent most of his life in Dublin. shops.name: Hodges Figgis
shops.description: Hodges Figgis is a long-operating bookshop in central Dublin, Ireland. Founded in 1768, it is probably the third-oldest functioning bookshop in the world, after the Livraria Bertrand of Lisbon (1732) and Pennsylvania's Moravian Book Shop (1745). shops.name: Marlay Park
shops.description: Marlay Park (Irish: Páirc Mharlaí) is a 121 hectares (300 acres) suburban public park located in the suburb of Rathfarnham in Dublin, Ireland. Lying about nine kilometres (5.6 miles) from Dublin city centre, the parkland comprises woodlands, ponds and walks. shops.name: Holman & Merriman Machine Shop
shops.description: The Holman & Merriman Machine Shop, also known as the Derby Shop, Goodnow Pail Factory, L. A. Carpenter Machine Shop, and Streeter Shop, is an historic industrial building at 63 Canal Street in Hinsdale, New Hampshire. This three-story brick building, built in 1837, is the only building with a clerestory roof in Hinsdale, and one of only four in the state. shops.name: Kilbride, County Wicklow
shops.description: Kilbride (Irish: Cill Bhríde), or Manor Kilbride, is a village, civil parish and electoral division in County Wicklow, Ireland, located at the western edge of the Wicklow Mountains in the barony of Talbotstown Lower.

shops.name: Conrad Gallagher
shops.description: Conrad Gallagher (born 12 March 1971) is an Irish-born chef/restaurateur from Letterkenny, County Donegal, based in Dubai since 2016. He was the youngest chef ever awarded a Michelin star at the time, for Peacock Alley in Dublin, at the age of 26 in 1998. shops.name: Craigavon mobile shop killings
shops.description: On 28 March 1991, a member of the Ulster Volunteer Force (UVF), a loyalist paramilitary group, shot dead three Catholic civilians at a mobile shop in Craigavon, County Armagh, Northern Ireland. The gunman boarded the van and shot two teenage girls working there, then forced a male customer to lie on the pavement and shot him also. shops.name: Deacon Abijah Richardson House
shops.description: The Deacon Abijah Richardson House is a historic house at 334 Hancock Road in Dublin, New Hampshire. Built in 1818 by the son of an early settler, it is a well-preserved example of an early 19th-century Cape-style farmhouse. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1983.
